plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LY11 re-reading and editing their own texts using agreed criteria; VC2E5LA05 complex sentences used for effect; VC2E5LA08 vocabulary for precision
plan.shape: before and after, name the move, punch it, revise: the model shows a paragraph revised with four moves, students name and practise each, then revise their own draft in colour
plan.criticalFeature: revising changes the meaning and impact for the reader; editing only fixes the errors
decisionPoints: the choice check: the biggest difference for the reader
the exit board: one named revision on a new paragraph
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Revising makes each move hit harder.
plan.catchUp: No full draft? Revise the paragraphs you have; the ARMS log works on any paragraph.

studentTools: Writing books with the complete draft and Session 1 revision plan
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: ARMS on the board: 1 Add, 2 Remove, 3 Move, 4 Swap
Revise = make it stronger. Edit = make it correct.

steps: Does it change the meaning or impact?
example.answer: edit: it only fixes a spelling mistake

items.prompt: Which change makes the biggest difference for the reader?
options: A sourced fact added after a claim.
items.explain: The fact makes the claim believable; the others barely change the meaning.

items.prompt: Ava says she revised. Find the problem and fix it.
work: I fixed three spelling mistakes and added a full stop.
items.answer: That is editing. Fix: add proof to paragraph 2 and swap a weak word.

slides.notes: Open the session. One line: today we take a good draft and make it great.

Print the Worksheet for everyone, the Extension for early finishers and the Supported Worksheet for those who need it. Coloured pencils for revisions. Drafts are on every second line, so there is room to revise.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to revise our draft so it is stronger for our reader.
successCriteria: I can name the four ARMS moves.
I can revise my writing using Add, Remove, Move and Swap.
I can vary my sentences so the key ones hit hardest.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: A first draft is just the start. Today you make yours stronger.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we all start.
The second one is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 is reachable for all; SC2 is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 is the stretch.

slides.title: Which draft would you rather read?
lines: Polar bears are in danger. This is bad. We should help them.
Polar bears are starving on shrinking ice. They cannot wait. We must act now.

notes.answer: the second - stronger words, a reason and a short punch
beats: SAY: Same writer, same idea. One is a first draft.
One has been revised.
ASK: Which would you rather read, first or second?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest, 1 or 2... show me.
EXPECT: 2
ASK: What did the writer change?
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: starving, shrinking, the short sentence, must
SAY: Yesterday's feedback tells you what to change. Today you change it.
trap: Fix: say spelling is editing, Thursday's job; today we change what it says.
notes.prep: Launch links the Session 1 revision plan to today. 3 minutes.

slides.meaning: To change your writing to make it stronger, not just correct.
slides.example: Swap bad for harmful. That is revising.

notes.answer: to change your writing to make it stronger, not just correct
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Revise. Say it with me. Revise.
SAY: To change your writing to make it stronger, not just correct.
SAY: Swap bad for harmful. That is revising.
ASK: Is fixing a spelling mistake revising or editing?
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: editing; it doesn't change the meaning
trap: thinking revise means rewrite it neatly.
Fix: ask did the meaning get stronger? If not, it's not revising.
notes.prep: Revise versus edit is the line between Sessions 2 and 3.

slides.title: Watch me find what to revise
slides.extract: Polar bears are in danger. This is bad. It is really, really bad. They need ice to hunt seals. We should probably help them.
highlights: This is bad. It is really, really bad.
They need ice to hunt seals.
slides.source: Sample draft, written for this session

notes.answer: swap in danger; remove the repeats; add proof; swap should probably for must
beats: READ it aloud once.
SAY: Every highlight is a spot I can make stronger.
POINT to This is bad. It is really, really bad.
SAY: Remove. It says nothing new. Out it goes.
POINT to They need ice to hunt seals.
SAY: Add. Who says so? According to Polar Bears International...
ASK: Should probably. Which move fixes it? 1 add, 2 remove, 3 move, 4 swap.
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 4, swap for must
trap: changing every word and losing the writer's voice.
Fix: student makes one move per weak spot only.
notes.stretch: Find the sentence that should move to the end.
notes.help: Start with Remove: cross out any sentence that repeats.
notes.prep: The model, part 1. Critical feature: revising changes the impact; editing only fixes errors.

slides.title: After: four moves later
slides.extract: Polar bears are starving. According to Polar Bears International, they hunt seals from the sea ice, and that ice is vanishing. They cannot wait. We must act now.
slides.source: Sample draft, revised for this session

notes.answer: swap, add, a short punch, swap
beats: READ the revised version aloud.
SAY: Same idea. Listen to how much harder it hits.
POINT to They cannot wait.
SAY: A long sentence, then three short words. The short one lands like a punch.
ASK: Which is stronger, before or after? Thumbs up for after.
3 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up
ASK: Name one move I made, and why it helps.
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: added a source so it's believable
trap: copying the model's words into their own draft.
Fix: student names the move, then makes it with their own words.
notes.stretch: Add a fronted Because-clause to one sentence.
notes.help: Make two moves only: one Add, one Swap.
notes.prep: The model, part 2. Sentence variety (VC2E5LA05): long build, short punch.

slides.title: Which move?
slides.pivot: read before and after aloud; what is different?
slides.followUp: cold call one student: how does it help the reader?

items.text: 'Litter is bad. It is so bad.' -> 'Litter chokes our creek.'
'We must act.' -> 'The IUCN lists bears as Vulnerable. We must act.'
The strongest reason moved to the last paragraph.
'It is very, very important.' -> 'It is urgent.'

trap: Fix: ask were words added or taken out? Student re-votes.
notes.stretch: Say how each move helps the reader.
notes.help: Count the words before and after: more means add, fewer means remove.
notes.prep: Guided naming of ARMS moves. SC1.

slides.title: Which change helps the reader most?

options.misconception: a synonym swap; the meaning barely changes

options.text: Adding a sourced fact after a claim.

notes.answer: B - proof makes the claim believable
beats: SAY: Three changes. Only one really changes things for the reader.
ASK: Which change helps the reader most?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: why doesn't A help much?
Less -> ask what does the reader learn from each? re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. Now the reader believes you. That's a real revision.
trap: pointing to C because neat work gets praised.
Fix: say neat comes on Publish Day; today is about meaning.
notes.prep: Decision point before students revise. Under 80% means the class revises one paragraph together on the board first.

slides.title: Punch it
slides.pivot: ask: what is the one thing this sentence builds to?
slides.followUp: cold call one board: read the long one, then your punch

items.text: Our bins overflow every Friday, and the wind spreads rubbish across the oval.
For thousands of years the ice carried bears to their food, and now it is melting away.
The creek behind our school used to croak with frogs, but now there is nothing.

say: A long sentence builds. A short one punches.
Write a short sentence to follow each long one.
trap: Fix: student counts words; five or fewer.
notes.stretch: Make your punch echo a word from the long sentence.
notes.help: Try: It has to stop. or Not anymore.

slides.title: Revise your draft
slides.task: Work through your Worksheet. Then revise your draft in colour: at least one Add, Remove, Move and Swap.

notes.answer: a draft revised in colour with all four moves
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Use your feedback from Session 1. Revise in colour, so you can see your changes.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Ask: which move is that? How does it help your reader?
ASK: How many of the four moves have you made so far?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 2 or more by halfway
trap: Fix: student finds one paragraph with no proof and adds some.
notes.stretch: Extension: revise for two readers, then test two endings.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture-clue choices, a first swap done, a frame.
notes.prep: Independent application on students' own drafts. The ARMS log is the evidence for SC2.

slides.extendedTask: a worksheet ending in an ARMS log, then the draft revised in colour

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Dogs at the beach is a thing people talk about. Some people think dogs are good. Dogs are good because they are good.
Make one revision. Name the ARMS move.

notes.answer: e.g. Remove the repeats; Add a reason: dogs need exercise
beats: SAY: A new paragraph that needs help. Make one revision.
ASK: Write one revision and the ARMS move.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: a real revision, correctly named
RECORD who only fixes spelling. Tomorrow's warm-up.
trap: Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new paragraph. One board per student.

notes.answer: open - Before: they need ice. After: according to NASA...
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can revise, not just edit?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.

RECORD each thumb down beside the exit boards.
ASK: Read your partner your best revision, before and after. Which move was it?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
